html:
SMTO-AUT-0023 — SMTO needs to know which Google account to update

GUID: 47abd8e0-d43d-5234-a4e8-5c383c821400
Slug: google-account-selection-required
Domain: AUT · Subsystem: google-workspace

What happened

  • A Google account is already connected through this Google app, so SMTO needs to know whether you're updating it or adding a new one. It won't quietly create a second copy, and nothing was saved from this attempt.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO to list your connected Google accounts so you can see which ones already exist. You need to know whether the Google account you want is already connected.
  2. To reconnect or add access to an account that's already listed, ask SMTO to connect again and point to that account, for example by typing @ and picking it. Pointing to the existing account makes SMTO update it instead of creating a duplicate.
  3. To add a different Google account, ask SMTO to connect it under a new, unused name of lowercase letters, numbers and underscores, such as work_google. A new name tells SMTO you really want a separate account, not an update.
  4. Open the new sign-in link, finish it within 10 minutes, and sign in with the Google account you meant. SMTO saves the connection only after Google confirms which account signed in.

What success looks like

  • The Google sign-in page says your email is connected, and the account appears once in SMTO's list of connected Google accounts.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send it to the person who manages SMTO. Don't delete existing Google account entries to get around this; other features may rely on them.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Google consent requires an explicit account_key: accounts already exist for this OAuth application, or the newly verified Google subject matches an already saved account.

What this means

  • Authorization needs an existing account key for an upgrade/reconnect, or a newly verified subject matches an already saved account. Authorization establishes a particular connection, account and scope. It neither expands operation permissions nor proves the outcome of a request already dispatched.

Why this can happen

  • Authorization needs an existing account key for an upgrade/reconnect, or a newly verified subject matches an already saved account.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare existing account keys, OAuth application and verified subject before starting or completing consent.

How to fix it

  • Call auth.google_connect with the existing account_key (from auth.google_accounts) when reconnecting or adding features, so the consent is bound to that record. Supply a different, unused account_key only to deliberately create another profile; without a key, GoogleOAuth refuses to start when accounts exist for the app and refuses to save a subject that is already stored.
  • Pass the existing account_key to auth.google_connect when reconnecting or adding features. Use a different key only to explicitly create another profile.

Retry and execution caution

  • Confirm account identity and required features before retrying.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended existing account key is updated, or a deliberately distinct new profile is created.

What not to do

  • Do not expose client secrets, tokens, codes or PKCE verifiers.
  • Do not switch accounts or repeat uncertain mutations automatically.

Technical notes

  • Authorization establishes a particular connection, account and scope. It neither expands operation permissions nor proves the outcome of a request already dispatched.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
